name: Gilla Band
label: Rough Trade
lede: Three school friends, a drummer, a techno cover and a singer who turned his own breakdown into a debut album, then came back with a name change and their most acclaimed record yet.

eras.title: Bad Strokes, worse emo
eras.text: Three of the four spent their teens in bands nobody remembers. The fourth was recruited when the singer stopped drumming, and the whole thing got a lot louder.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Line of Best Fit: Gilla Band
years.h: Harrows: [[Dara Kiely|e9d78b78-13c2-43eb-a11e-681f57172def]], [[Alan Duggan|ef76acf1-141f-4d57-bb3f-1f9286afebee]] and [[Daniel Fox|2270dc4f-930e-430d-abf3-8c3e0e59e858]] at 16
years.p: Kiely drummed, Duggan played guitar and Fox played bass in a school band the members now describe as a poor imitation of the Strokes. Nothing was released beyond some Myspace and YouTube uploads.
years.xp:
Harrows never got a deal. The recordings that exist were uploaded to YouTube and Myspace, and the members have since described the band as a bad copy of the Strokes.

The Line of Best Fit also reports a short-lived emo band called Surface, with Kiely still on drums. When it folded he moved to the microphone and the band went looking for a drummer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Quietus: Mysterious Handsome Men
years.h: Girl Band forms in Dublin with Adam Faulkner on drums
years.p: Kiely swaps the kit for the mic, Faulkner takes the stool, and the band names itself after Duggan asked a woman in a bar what she thought of it.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the start to July 2011. The Quietus has Duggan saying the aim was 'just not your average indie band', getting as far from that as possible.

Kiely's account of the name: Duggan turned to a woman at a bar and asked what she thought of Girl Band as a name.

eras.title: Small city, big racket
eras.text: Dublin is small enough that bands share rehearsal rooms and members. Girl Band spent three years releasing singles on a local label and turning a techno cover into their calling card.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Quietus: Mysterious Handsome Men
years.h: 'In My Head': first single, on Any Other City
years.p: The debut single comes out on the Dublin label Any Other City, recorded by the band themselves.
years.xp:
The band recorded their first single and EP themselves, and told The Quietus they cared most about control: 'It sounds exactly how it's meant to.'

Fox on the local scene, same interview: Dublin's small, so you get to know the other bands quickly.

years.h: France 98 EP, recorded live
years.p: The band's first EP arrives on Any Other City on October 11 as a 12-inch and download.

years.src: Wikipedia: Why They Hide Their Bodies · Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Quietus: Mysterious Handsome Men
yt: Live at the Old Blue Last, London, Jan 2015
years.h: A rock band covers a Blawan techno track, and it gets them a UK tour
years.p: Their eight-minute version of Blawan's 'Why They Hide Their Bodies Under My Garage?' spreads the name well past Dublin.
years.xp:
The cover was recorded for the Quarter Inch Collective compilation. The Quietus notes it drew attention partly for how Kiely pronounces 'garage'. Wikipedia says the exposure led to UK dates in April 2013.

NPR's Otis Hart, quoted on Wikipedia, noted how rare it is for a rock band to cover techno. He said the band's version builds tension slowly and climaxes halfway through with distorted guitar, where Blawan's original repeats a sample over a constant beat for more than six minutes.

years.src: AOL: Gilla Band · Wikipedia: Gilla Band
years.h: 'Lawman' becomes the song people ask about
years.p: A run of limited 7-inches on Any Other City includes 'Lawman', the single AOL later calls the band's breakout.
years.xp:
Girl Band put out several limited 7-inch singles through Any Other City in 2014. AOL's profile picks 'Lawman' as the breakout among them.

It became a staple of their sets for years, and the band were still playing it at Vicar Street in 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · Wikipedia: Holding Hands with Jamie
years.h: Geoff Travis signs them to Rough Trade after repeated shows
years.p: Travis, the label's founder, watched several Girl Band gigs before offering a deal. The band kept full creative control and production.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Travis wanted to amplify what they were doing on a bigger scale, and that the band kept complete creative autonomy and production control. That set the pattern: every Girl Band and Gilla Band album since has been self-produced.

eras.title: Holding Hands with Jamie
eras.text: A debut that documents its singer's breakdown in order, a US touring push, and then a stretch of cancelled dates that ended with a hiatus.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Thin Air
years.h: The Early Years collects the singles for Rough Trade
years.p: The label puts the Any Other City run and the Blawan cover on one 12-inch, CD and download.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the EP to April 21, 2015. The Line of Best Fit's interviewer places it around 2014, so the exact date is in questions.

years.src: The Quietus: Shakedown The Breakdown · Rolling Stone: Holding Hands · Wikipedia: Gilla Band
years.h: Holding Hands with Jamie, a self-produced debut
years.p: Engineered by Liam Mulvaney and Jamie Hyland and mixed live on an analog desk. It reaches number 11 in Ireland.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone said it sounded 'like it was recorded in a meat locker under a fallout shelter', and called Kiely a 'dryly funny' chronicler of everyday hate. The Guardian called it 'an unbroken series of thumping, crashing songs'.

The video for 'Paul' arrived in August, a few weeks ahead of the record.

years.big: Lyrics finished on the last day of recording
q: The whole album is based on this psychotic episode I had two years ago.
years.src: The Quietus: Shakedown The Breakdown
years.h: The album is Dara Kiely's psychotic episode, in order
years.p: Kiely told The Quietus the record follows the breakdown he had two years earlier, through to hospital. His mother told him to write anything.
years.xp:
The album runs in chronological order through the episode and ends with 'Witchdoctor', which references a period when Kiely wore a woman's jacket and felt elated. After a couple of months in hospital he found meditation and told The Quietus he was 'the happiest I've been, within reason'.

His mother's advice, he said, was 'Just write anything', including the sentence 'I can't think of anything to write' if that was all there was.

years.src: The Quietus: Shakedown The Breakdown
years.h: Savages tour delayed by visas; they pick up Dave Grohl's beers in DC
years.p: Visa problems cost them a January US run supporting Savages. When they did tour, New York shows drew a better crowd than an Irish band had reason to expect.
years.xp:
Per The Quietus, they left one American venue in Washington with beers Dave Grohl had left behind, then drove on to the next show.

New York rooms were 70 to 80 percent full, a result the band did not expect.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Talkies · Hot Press: Choice Music Prize · AOL: Gilla Band
years.h: Cancelled shows, then a year off
years.p: AOL reports tours in 2015 and 2017 were cancelled or cut short over wellness concerns. Wikipedia has the band stopping for about a year.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's account of The Talkies says Kiely's mental health worsened and shows were cancelled, followed by a year-long hiatus in 2017. The band reconvened in February 2018.

Hot Press put it as the band stepping quietly out of the spotlight after a run of cancelled tour dates.

eras.title: A haunted house in Laois
eras.text: They came back with a mansion, a key of A, and an album that opens on a recorded panic attack.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Talkies
years.h: They reconvene at Ballintubbert House, County Laois
years.p: Fox found the mansion through his engineering contacts and got it cheap. Recording continued at Sonic Studios in Dublin and Grand Street in Brooklyn.
years.xp:
Fox said there were lots of good rooms and that not being in a studio meant they got the house 'for buttons'. Duggan described the aim as an audio representation of the mansion itself.

They recorded everything in the key of A around repeating motifs, with Marvin Gaye and Kendrick Lamar on the stereo. Kiely avoided pronouns in the lyrics: 'I' sounded arrogant to him and 'you' accusatory.

years.h: 'Shoulderblades': first new song in four years
years.p: Girl Band come back with a single on June 7 and a video for it.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Talkies · The Line of Best Fit: Gilla Band · Far Out: Talking The Talkies
years.h: The Talkies: Pitchfork gives it an 8.0
years.p: Peaks at 11 in Ireland and 73 in the UK. NME gives it five stars. 'Going Norway' and 'Salmon of Knowledge' come out as singles.
years.xp:
Kiely completed a peer-support course on mental health at DCU around this time. He told The Line of Best Fit that the panic attack captured on 'Prolix' is followed by a mindfulness breathing outro, 'Ereignis'.

The band also recorded 'Aibohphobia' by learning it backwards, recording that, then reversing the tape. The lyrics are palindromic.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Talkies · Hot Press: Choice Music Prize
years.h: Vicar Street live LP; The Talkies shortlisted for the Choice Music Prize
years.p: Recordings from the band's Dublin shows at Vicar Street, on the sold-out autumn 2019 tour, are released as a live LP.
years.xp: Hot Press's March 2020 piece on the shortlist says Girl Band's debut 'revolutionised the Irish music scene'.

eras.title: Gilla, and a studio band
eras.text: A new name, a record written in lockdown rather than a rehearsal room, and their first full US tour.

years.big: From a place of naivety and ignorance
years.src: Stereogum: Girl Band change their name
years.h: Girl Band become Gilla Band, and apologise
years.p: The band said the old name was chosen without much thought and misgendered its bearers. 'Gilla' is a given name from old Irish.
years.xp:
Stereogum reported the statement: 'We apologise for choosing a misgendered name in the first place and to anyone who has been hurt or affected by it.'

They said they would no longer perform or release records as Girl Band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Most Normal · The Line of Best Fit: Gilla Band · AOL: Gilla Band
years.h: Most Normal, made in the studio for a change
years.p: Recorded at Sonic Studios and their rehearsal space, and produced by Fox, with lap steel and organ in the mix. Number 30 in Ireland.
years.xp:
The Irish Times' Eamon Sweeney called Kiely 'often hilariously funny'. Pitchfork's Laura Snapes described the sound as 'unrelenting' with an 'indignant, surreal mania'.

Fox told The Line of Best Fit lockdown gave them time to be more playful. 'Post Ryan' took about a year to finish.

years.src: The Thin Air: A Band Apart · Wikipedia: Most Normal
years.h: First proper US tour, with several sold-out dates
years.p: The Thin Air calls the February 2023 run a success, and reports the band were already working on a fourth album.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the first full US tour to the album's release in 2022. The Thin Air places a sold-out American tour in February 2023. Both are in questions.

eras.title: Pugnello
eras.text: Four years, three Dublin studios, a drum machine, a death in the family and a diagnosis. The critics agreed it was their best.

years.src: The Line of Best Fit: Pugnello announcement · DIY: Pugnello review
years.h: 'Giraffe': first taste of album four
years.p: The single lands in May 2026 and later sits at track eight on Pugnello.
years.xp: DIY described it as morphing into 'a techno shuffle of grotesque proportions'.

years.src: Rough Trade: Pugnello announcement · Stereogum: Pugnello announcement
years.h: Album announced with 'Placeholder' and a Power Rangers confession
years.p: Kiely said the song examines his comfort distractions. At six, he was laughed at at a Christian summer camp for saying he wanted to be a Power Ranger.
years.xp:
Kiely said in the statement that he was 'injecting a lethal dose of nothing' and 'blaring a dangerous amount of Coldplay'. He added he had never forgiven the camp leaders about the Power Rangers.

The video was directed by Cuan Roche.

q: We just make music to impress each other really.
years.src: Metacritic: Pugnello · Rough Trade: Pugnello announcement · DIY: Gilla Band talk · DIY: Pugnello review · Beats Per Minute: Pugnello · The Guardian: Pugnello review
years.h: Pugnello: Pitchfork scores it 8.8
years.p: Pitchfork's review, dated September 24, calls it the band's 'most methodical and charged album to date', per Metacritic. The Guardian gives five stars.
years.xp:
Recorded from 2022 to 2026 at Hellfire, Yellow Door Music Studio and Sonic Studios in Dublin. Produced by the band, recorded and mixed by Fox. The Erica Synths Perkons HD-01 drum machine sits at the centre of it, and DIY reports Neil Young's Trans as an influence on the final track.

DIY and Beats Per Minute say it was written after the death of Kiely's father and around his schizophrenia diagnosis, which he had avoided for years. Metacritic lists 87 across 11 reviews. Beats Per Minute gave it 92 percent. The Guardian's Alexis Petridis called it the work of a band 'audibly and thrillingly out on their own'.
